newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian health workers end 15-day-old strike.
newsitem.headline: Colombian health workers end 15-day-old strike.

text.p: Colombian health workers agreed to end a 15-day-old strike on Tuesday that had brought near paralysis to state-run hospitals. But union officials vowed that more labour unrest would erupt next week.

Spokesmen for the medical workers' union known as ASMEDAS said they had agreed to lift their work stoppage in exchange for a 36 percent pay hike -- retroactive to Jan. 1 -- for the 120,000 doctors, nurses and other employees in government-run hospitals and clinics across the country.
Most of the hospitals had been offering only emergency services since the strike began on June 3.
A pact sealing the wage deal, and officially ending the strike, was to be signed at the presidential palace Tuesday afternoon, union and government officials said.

Wilson Borja, head of the state workers' union known as Fenaltrase, said the successful end of the heatlh workers' strike would not affect Fenaltrase's plans to stage another nationwide work stoppage later this month.
The new strike by the union, which represents about 800,000 state workers, would be held to protest against the government's privatisation programme and neo-liberal economic policies, Borja said.
"We're still organising the strike because the government plans to lay off workers and because of its privatisation programme," Borja told Reuters in a telephone interview.

Fenaltrase staged a one-day strike that was supported by state oil workers on June 11, in support of health workers and to campaign against policies that its left-leaning leaders maintain have been dictated to Colombia by the World Bank and International Monetary Fund.
Borja has said the new strike, which will take place sometime beginning next week, may last indefinitely.
